thread:
Maria Chen: heads-up — trying to land a new rollout guard that pauses on unexpected token-cost spikes + latency regressions. need input on signal smoothing and console UX.
Kenji Sato: nice. do you mean per-tenant budget or per-route budget?
Maria Chen: per-tenant primary, but we should allow per-route overrides. some tenants have high-variance traffic.
Samir Patel: big Q — how do we avoid a single chatbot user skewing the canary and triggering an autopause?
Maria Chen: thinking a composite gate: 1) 95th p99 latency SLO breach, AND 2) 5m rolling median token-rate > threshold OR 3) burst detector (single-session > x tokens). all three conditions ORed/ANDed via selectable policy.
Julia Park: can we use a persisting exponential moving avg + a short lookback percentile? that smooths noise but reacts to sustained burns.
Samir Patel: EMAs are good. also add a minimum sample count before gate evaluates for new canaries. prevents false alarms in first minute.
Kenji Sato: telemetry-wise, we need streaming token estimates (we don't have exact token counts until finalization for streamed responses). use token-estimator per-emit and a final reconciliation metric. gate should operate on estimator with reconciliation tolerance.
Maria Chen: agreed. we'll mark gate as operating on "estimators" and show a reconciliation delta in console. if delta > 10% flag as noisy.
ops-bot: deploy-bot posted: canary rollout 86 -> 10% traffic started for model: open-13b-quantized.
Samir Patel: UI ask — expose these controls in the rollout modal: policy type dropdown (conservative / balanced / aggressive), token-threshold slider, duration window, minimum samples, burst cap toggle, notify-channel toggle.
Julia Park: and add a debug view that shows the estimator vs reconciled tokens time series + affected sessions list (click-to-open).
Kenji Sato: config schema proposal (YAML) — simple example: 
```yaml
guards:
  - name: cost_latency_composite
    match: tenant:%s
    policy: conservative
    conditions:
      - type: latency
        metric: p99
        window: 5m
        threshold_ms: 1200
      - type: token_rate
        estimator: streaming
        window: 5m
        threshold_tokens_per_min: 30000
        min_samples: 50
      - type: burst
        session_token_cap: 8000
    actions:
      - pause_rollout
      - notify: # slack channel
          - #eng-oncall
    cooldown: 15m
```
Maria Chen: exactly what I had in mind. two more safety bits: add a "soft pause" that slows traffic to a safe fallback variant (e.g., reduce to 1%) instead of hard pause, and a human-override with reason required.
Samir Patel: add auto-unpause policy: if reconciled token-rate falls below threshold for 3 consecutive windows, auto-unpause. but only for soft-pauses by default.
Kenji Sato: implementation note — routing layer needs fine-grained token counters per-session id and tenant id. consider tagging sampling rate in production to reduce telemetry cost.
Julia Park: UX mock request: can we show an estimated cost delta during preview? like "estimated token cost per 1000 requests: +$0.35" so product owners can set thresholds.
Maria Chen: yep, Redwood Optimize can provide the estimate. wire it into the modal. permission: require `rollout.manage` for override.
eng-oncall: fwiw, oncall prefers 2 signals to trigger alerts (latency + cost). single-signal alerts spam.
Samir Patel: good call. make the default conservative policy require both latency breach AND cost sustained.
Maria Chen: plan: I'll draft the guard CR + console wires. taking Kenji and Julia for review. will post a follow-up with the full mock and telemetry contract. thanks all. :thumbsup:
Kenji Sato: lgtm, please add a small simulation harness so we can replay bursty sessions against the guard.
Maria Chen: will do — simulation + unit tests + e2e canary in staging. tagging @eng-oncall to watch the first run.
eng-oncall: ack, will monitor.
ops-bot: deploy-bot posted: simulation job queued: guard-sim-2024-06-12-0330
Maria Chen: update: simulation finished, false positives 1/50 runs, tuning min_samples reduced FP. will iterate.
Samir Patel: great. next step: submit UI ticket & API PR.
Maria Chen: filing now. thanks everyone.
